svg.text: FEATURE FLAGS — HOW ONE isFeatureEnabled() CALL DECIDES
FOUR GATES, IN THIS ORDER — the first "no" wins
called on every request — must stay a few nanoseconds
GATE 3 are there any targeting rules ?
no rules ⇒ the rollout applies to EVERYONE
GATE 4 does ANY rule match this user ?
first match short-circuits the loop — OR, never AND
and it will return true for THIS user every time
ONE FLAG, FIVE USERS — the same gates, worked through
Read the 25% carefully: it is 25% OF THE TARGETED COHORT, not 25% of all users.
Targeting narrows the population first; the percentage then samples inside whatever survived.
4 of 5 users are in the cohort; 2 of those 4 are inside the 25% sample. u-3007 never even gets a bucket computed.
THE BUCKET LINE — why ramping never takes the feature away
still OFF at 25% — turns on as the ramp reaches their bucket
Because the test is bucket < percentage, raising 5% → 25% → 100% only ever ADDS users. Nobody
who already had the feature loses it mid-ramp — that monotonicity is free, and it is the point. ✓
Rolling BACK is not symmetric: dropping 25% → 5% does remove it from buckets 5..24. For a true
"never take it back" guarantee you need a sticky assignment stored per user, not a recomputed hash.
Also: change the featureId string and EVERY bucket reshuffles — renaming a flag silently re-randomises the cohort.

g.text: WHY THIS EXACT ORDER — and not any other
Kill switch first. During an incident you want ONE boolean that stops the feature for everyone,
without reasoning about rules or percentages. Put it anywhere else and the kill is conditional.
Targeting before rollout. "50% of beta users" and "beta users among the 50%" are different
populations. Narrow first, then sample — that is the semantics people expect from the UI.
Cheapest check first is a bonus, not the reason: correctness dictates this order, performance agrees.

svg.text: COST & THE THINGS THIS PATH DOES NOT DO
One CHM get + at most R rule checks + one hash ⇒ O(R), no I/O, no lock, no allocation…
…except it DOES allocate: two Strategy objects are constructed on every single call.
No evaluation is recorded — AuditLog exists in the package but is never written to, so you
cannot answer "was this user in the experiment last Tuesday?" — fatal for A/B analysis.
Also absent: variants beyond boolean (multivariate), scheduled ramps, per-environment overrides, and a config source.
